clue.text: Dicky is tipped nothing, and gets frustrated

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for shaky or unsound, so the following letters are in poor order and must be rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, the round letter O

explanation.surface: Someone called Dicky is given no tip and ends up fed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name but is the anagram signal: IS TIPPED plus O (nothing) plus AND are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Being let down when hopes are thwarted is the same as having expectations unmet.

clue.text: Drawing a drink

explanation.surface: Someone sketches while having a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught is the act of drawing or pulling something (as in a draught horse), and also a swallow or serving of liquor.

clue.text: A soldier's poesy maybe

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word poesy is only one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A trooper's verse, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: A sepoy was an Indian soldier serving under British command.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a sepoy was an Indian infantryman in a European-led army.

clue.text: Second or third pleasurable experience in a punt? Definitely not

parts.note: coming second or third in a race is finishing in a place
a kick is a thrill, as in getting a kick out of something

explanation.surface: A trip on a punt that comes in second or third and is no fun at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a punt as a river boat; in rugby and American football a punt is a kick dropped from the hands, the opposite of a kick from the ball placed on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A kick taken with the ball resting on the ground is the contrasting style to a punt, which is volleyed from the hands.

clue.text: Divine Scandinavian has circular racket

parts.note: the letter O is round, a circular shape
a din is a loud noise or racket

explanation.surface: A Nordic god makes a noise that goes round and round.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief god of Norse mythology, a deity of Scandinavia.

clue.text: Horse given a drink in Japan

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
saki is a variant spelling of sake, Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: A horse is offered a drink while in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Japan' defines the answer as a place in Japan, and the drink is fittingly Japanese.
explanation.definitionFit: Nagasaki is a port city on the Japanese island of Kyushu.

clue.text: Boy gets a girl

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad finds himself a girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a female first name.

clue.text: Synthetic material sounds foolish on ice-cream

indicators.note: sounds says the answer is spoken like the following phrase

parts.note: foolish is silly and an ice-cream is a cone, silly placed before cone

explanation.surface: A man-made substance seems a daft thing to put on an ice-cream.
explanation.walkthrough: Said out loud, SILLY CONE matches the polymer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Silicone is a man-made polymer used in sealants and implants.

clue.text: Bones shaken in 19

indicators.note: shaken means the letters of the answer to clue 19 are jumbled

parts.note: the answer to 19 across, meaning behind

explanation.surface: Bones rattled inside a numbered item.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterna is the plural of sternum, the breastbone.

clue.text: A very quiet borough but attractive

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quiet
Ealing is a borough of west London

explanation.surface: A hushed London district that nonetheless has its charms.
explanation.walkthrough: EALING is a borough in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something appealing has charm that draws people in, so it is pleasing.

clue.text: Painted one who blinked on discovery in Belmont

definitions.text: Painted one who blinked on discovery in Belmont

parts.words: Painted one who blinked on discovery in Belmont
parts.note: in The Merchant of Venice the Prince of Arragon opens the silver casket at Portia's house in Belmont and finds the portrait of a blinking fool

explanation.surface: A portrait subject who flinched when found at a country house.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Arragon exclaims 'the portrait of a blinking idiot'; blinking is also a mild British intensifier, so the painted figure blinks only in a pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The picture found in Arragon's casket is described in the play as that of a blinking fool, a simpleton.

clue.text: Old man sounds as if he's involved in domestic hot water

indicators.note: sounds signals that the answer is spoken like the slang for an old man

parts.note: geezer is British slang for an old man

explanation.surface: An old man seems to be in hot water at home.
explanation.walkthrough: In British use a geyser is a gas water heater in the home, not only a hot spring; pronounced GEEZER in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a geyser is a gas-fired appliance heating household water.

clue.text: Frame unorthodox replies about article

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the article
unorthodox means the word replies is rearranged into an unusual order

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Unconventional answers concerning a piece of writing are put in a frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unorthodox' turns REPLIES into ESPLIER, and 'about' puts it around A.
explanation.definitionFit: An espalier is a trellis on which fruit trees are trained flat, a supporting lattice.

clue.text: Smell it? Send back the meal

indicators.note: send back means the letters are put back to front

parts.note: niff is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A diner sniffs the dish and returns it to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send back' turns NIFFIT around; NIFF is British slang for a pong.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffin is a light midday lunch, chiefly in India.

clue.text: Beast in myth liable to suffer unfair change

indicators.note: in places the beast inside the myth

parts.note: a fable is a myth or legend
a ram is a male sheep, a beast

explanation.surface: A creature in a legend is prone to be changed unjustly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' is printed but the sense needs 'charge': to be framed is to be falsely accused.
explanation.definitionFit: To be framed is to be set up for a crime one did not commit, so a framable person could be falsely accused.

clue.text: Approve the French housemaster in this state

parts.note: to OK something is to approve it
la is French for the, feminine
house is abbreviated HO and master is MA, Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A school housemaster from France gets the nod in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housemaster' looks like one school post but splits as HO (house) and MA (Master of Arts).
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma is one of the states of the USA.

clue.text: Coming from the South to first-class climbing country

parts.note: austral means southern, from the south

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the letters go upwards, read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Arriving from the south to a top-notch mountaineering land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns A1 upward, giving IA; the figure 1 serves as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is a nation occupying its own continent.

clue.text: Blare can upset this goose

indicators.note: upset means the letters of blare can are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A loud trumpeting can startle a goose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' points the definition at the goose named by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The barnacle goose is a black and white Arctic-breeding goose.

clue.text: But a judge who assumed this didn't give bird!

definitions.text: But a judge who assumed this didn't give bird!

parts.words: But a judge who assumed this didn't give bird!
parts.note: a British judge put on a black square cap before passing a death sentence, so he was not handing out prison time, which is slang 'bird'

explanation.surface: A judge who donned a certain cap was not sending anyone to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is British slang for a jail term (from rhyming slang 'birdlime' for time); the answer is also a warbler, hence the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The black cap was worn by judges imposing capital punishment, and the name is also a small songbird.

clue.text: Baseball player should strike repeatedly

explanation.surface: A hitter in a ballgame ought to keep swinging.
explanation.definitionFit: A batter is the hitter at the plate in baseball, and to batter is to pound with blow after blow.

clue.text: Like a bird's behind

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Resembling the rear end of a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird's behind' reads as a tail, but behind is the definition and 'Like a bird' gives AS TERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is a nautical word for at the rear or back of a ship.

clue.text: Girl eager to get material

parts.note: Nan is a girl's name
keen means eager

explanation.surface: A keen young woman sets out to acquire fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth originally from Nanjing.

clue.text: He leaves the fence hanging back

indicators.note: leaves means the letters of he depart from the word the

parts.note: a railing is a fence of bars

explanation.surface: A man walks off, leaving the fence sagging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes HE out of THE, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: Trailing means lagging behind, following at the rear.

clue.text: Article below left one flexible

indicators.note: below in a down clue places the article under the other letters

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece is supple and sits beneath the one on the left.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe describes a body that is supple and bends easily.

clue.text: 10's island, no end popular

indicators.note: no end means the final letter of the island is dropped

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: The fool's island home, endlessly popular.
explanation.walkthrough: '10's' reads as '10 is', pointing to IDIOT, the answer to 10 across; 'no end' cuts the final E from CRETE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cretin is an insulting term for a fool or simpleton.

clue.text: This guarantees all the players full employment

definitions.text: This guarantees all the players full employment

parts.words: This guarantees all the players full employment
parts.note: a musical direction telling the whole orchestra or ensemble to play together, so no player sits idle

explanation.surface: A scheme that keeps every member of a team in work.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like economics or a sports squad; it is the score marking for everyone to play.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti, Italian for all, marks a passage played by the full ensemble.

clue.text: Not a good fellow, East — a rebel in fact

parts.note: a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably

explanation.surface: An eastern scoundrel who really was an insurgent.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450; 'in fact' signals a real historical rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Cade headed the 1450 uprising against Henry VI, a real-life insurgent.

clue.text: Note reflection of mineral in brilliant display

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: reflection of means the mineral is seen as in a mirror, back to front

parts.note: talc is a soft mineral

explanation.surface: A musical tone mirrored in a gem's dazzling show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflection of' turns TALC into CLAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is conspicuous success or a dazzling show of flair.

clue.text: Sweet girl

explanation.surface: A lovely young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlotte is a pudding of fruit in a mould of bread or sponge, and Charlotte is a woman's name.

clue.text: Fresh formation for soldiers by age-group

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are a corps of British army soldiers
a generation is people of the same age

explanation.surface: A new military formation is created by grouping troops by age.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Regeneration is renewal, forming tissue or structures anew.
